message:
docs(update): settle the four open sections, and stop leaning on taskkill /T

Section 4 was written as four holes waiting on a decision. The decisions came,
and two of them change design that was already written down.

Transport and provenance: a WinHTTP HTTPS client built for the update path
alone -- the existing directory client, auth and log upload stay as they are.
The manifest carries platform, version, size, SHA-256 and artifact identity
under one detached signature, verified against a public key in the binary.
ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256, because BCrypt/CNG, java.security.Signature and
node:crypto all ship it; Ed25519 is out on uneven CNG support. No turning off
certificate validation, no ignoring certificate errors, no HTTPS-to-HTTP
redirect. This is not Authenticode and does not buy publisher trust.

Android keeps its key. The shipped APK's certificate and the local
debug.keystore fingerprint match exactly, so updates go in place and app data
survives -- the earlier "switch keys, uninstall, lose data" passage now covers
only the case where that key is unavailable.

Two corrections to what was already written. Killing the process tree is not
something to route around by placing the updater elsewhere; the stop step now
names each of the six executables and confirms them individually, which also
takes the /T enumeration question out of the design entirely. And version
comparison cannot be a shared header when it has to hold across JS, C++ and
Kotlin -- it is a contract plus one set of test vectors all three read, with
extraction confined to C++.

Design settled, not cleared to ship: signing keys, the keystore's home, the
production domain and the nginx vhost are all separate approvals, kept apart
in 4.5.

Documentation only -- no product, CMake or gradle change, no build or test run.
